summary: Adding a CSV export of orders to the admin area of the same Next.js store, with a date-range filter and an API route.

history.content: Admins need to export orders to CSV from /admin/orders. Columns: order id, date, customer name, email, total, status. Filter by date range.
Let me find the admin orders page and how orders are queried.
I'll add a CSV serializer and an API route the admin page can link to.
And a test for the serializer.

PASS  src/lib/export/ordersCsv.test.ts
  ✓ header row
  ✓ one row per order
  ✓ total has two decimals

Test Suites: 1 passed, 1 total
Tests:       3 passed, 3 total
Snapshots:   0 total
The route works: GET /api/admin/orders/export?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD returns orders.csv with the six columns, and the tests pass. Nothing on /admin/orders links to it yet.
I opened it in Excel and the dates look weird, some show as 3/4 and some as 4/3. The names with commas are a separate ticket, leave those for now
That's locale-dependent formatting from toLocaleDateString. I'll switch to ISO 8601 so every tool reads it the same way.
